newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling slides amid nervous trade.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling slides amid nervous trade.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling took a downturn against the dollar on Wednesday triggered by strong demand which sent panic waves across the interbank market, commercial bank dealers said.
Kenya's Central Bank posted a mean shilling rate of 53.72 against the dollar compared to 53.45 on Tuesday, while against the pound the shilling was posted at a mean of 88.01 from 87.69.
"We believe there was a large order from one bank but in my opinion it was executed quite unprofessionally, which has triggered this panic in the market," said a bank treasurer.
"We're now doing about 54.30/80," one shilling lower than Tuesday, another dealer said.

Some dealers speculated that investors could have panicked after seeing foreign investors pull out of the market on Monday, largely because they were unsuccessful at their bids at the treasury bill aution last week.
They said many of them quoted rates above 20 percent while the going rate on the main 91-day category of T-bills is 19.667 percent.
Apart from easing T-bill rates, the market is entering a nervous period with the 1997/98 financial budget scheduled for June 19 and a general election later in the year.
The money market was liquid. Overnight rates were quoted at between 8-9 percent unchanged.
